description: DUT advertises an MSS != 536 in active-OPEN SYN when its receive MSS differs from the RFC 1122 §4.2.2.6 default
approach:
[Objective]
If DUT can receive larger segments than the 536 default, it MUST tell the peer — otherwise the peer wastes bandwidth.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. DUT receive MSS configured to non-536 value (e.g. 1460).
2. Tester (UT) → DUT: active OPEN call.
3. DUT → Tester: SYN.
4. Observation: SYN's MSS option ≠ 536.

[Pass condition]
DUT-emitted MSS option carries the non-default value.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_timeout — no DUT SYN with non-default MSS

verdicts.Fail_timeout: No DUT SYN with non-default MSS
